scenario: After a long-term imprisonment and while awaiting a parole decision, a convicted thief wants to organise a foundation for young victims of crime. I am the president of the agency who decides about the foundation. The founder would donate 250,000 dollars to the foundation. However, he asks that the foundation would be named after himself, helping clear his name. His victim opposes such a foundation and considers it immoral. If I approve and accept the money for the foundation, crime victims will benefit from the 250,000 dollars. If I do nothing, the money will be lost.
entities: 1 agency president,1 convicted thief who wants to found and name the foundation after himself,1 victim of the thief who opposes the foundation,an unknown number of young victims of crime who would potentially benefit from the foundation,I
outcomes: The 250,000 dollars is not donated to support young victims of crime
Young victims of crime do not receive the foundation's help
The convicted thief does not receive public recognition through a foundation bearing his name
The victim is spared the harm of seeing the convicted thief honored
